title: Generic field of an injective ind-etale domain algebra
statement:
Let $A\to C$ be an injective homomorphism of commutative integral domains, and suppose it is ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and $L=\operatorname{Frac}(C)$, with the induced inclusion $K\subseteq L$. Then the canonical map
$$ (A\setminus\{0\})^{-1}C=K\otimes_A C\longrightarrow L $$
is an isomorphism, and $L/K$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. In particular, for any field $F$ and unital map $f:C\to F$ whose restriction to $A$ is injective, $f$ is injective and extends uniquely to a field embedding $L\hookrightarrow F$.

source.place: Tag 0BSD, section-ramification, generic-fibre injectivity in its displayed diagram; auxiliary field calculation from proetale.tex Tag 092Q and algebra.tex Tag 00U3.

proof.text: Write $u:A\to C$ and $S=A\setminus\{0\}$. The tensor product $B=K\otimes_A C$ identifies with $S^{-1}C$: the mutually inverse maps are $(a/s)\otimes c\mapsto u(a)c/u(s)$ and $c/u(s)\mapsto (1/s)\otimes c$. These respect the tensor balancing and fraction relations, and their composites fix the displayed generators. The map $j:B\to L$ sends $c/u(s)$ to the same fraction in $L$. It is injective: if this fraction is zero, $c=0$ since $u(s)\ne0$ and $C$ is a domain. Thus $B$ is a nonzero domain and contains $K$.

source.place: Tag 0BSD, section-ramification, generic-field diagram; explicit tensor/fraction calculation

proof.text: Apply ind-etale stability to the base change $A\to K$. It gives that $K\to B$ is ind-etale, hence weakly etale. Therefore every finitely generated $K$-subalgebra of $B$ is finite etale, by the weakly-etale field theorem. No finite-generation hypothesis on $C$ or $B$ is used.

For $b\in B$, the subalgebra $D=K[b]\subseteq B$ is generated by one element, hence is etale by step 2. The classification of etale algebras over a field gives a $K$-algebra isomorphism $D\cong\prod_{r=1}^n E_r$ with finite separable field extensions $E_r/K$. Since $D$ is a nonzero domain, $n\ne0$ and $n$ cannot exceed one: for $n\ge2$ a coordinate idempotent $e$ and $1-e$ would be nonzero with product zero. Thus $D$ is a finite separable field extension of $K$.

If $b\ne0$, its inverse in the field $K[b]$ also belongs to $B$. Consequently $B$ is a field. Every $b\in B$ is algebraic and separable over $K$, because it belongs to the finite separable extension $K[b]/K$ of step 3: the kernel of evaluation $K[T]\to K[b]\hookrightarrow B$ is the same as for $K[T]\to K[b]$, so the minimal polynomial is unchanged. Hence $B/K$ is separable algebraic in the cited definition.

source.place: Tag 00U3, lemma-etale-over-field; elementary consequences of the one-factor case

proof.text: The injection $j:B\to L$ is surjective. Indeed, any $c/d\in L$ with $c,d\in C$ and $d\ne0$ is $j((c/1)(d/1)^{-1})$, since $d/1\ne0$ by step 1 and $B$ is a field by step 4. Thus the canonical map is an isomorphism over $K$. The equality of evaluation kernels under this $K$-isomorphism transports the separable algebraicity of every element of $B$ to every element of $L$.

source.place: Tag 0BSD, section-ramification, generic-field diagram; explicit fraction surjectivity

proof.text: Finally let $f:C\to F$ be as stated. For $s\in S$, $f(u(s))\ne0$ by injectivity on $A$, so $h:B\to F$, $h(c/u(s))=f(c)/f(u(s))$, is a well-defined unital homomorphism: cross-multiplication of fraction relations verifies well-definedness and the ring operations. It is injective because a nonzero element $b$ of the field $B$ has $h(b)h(b^{-1})=1$. Its restriction to $C$ is $f$, and $C\hookrightarrow B$ is injective, so $f$ is injective. Composing $h$ with $j^{-1}$ gives the required embedding $L\hookrightarrow F$. Uniqueness holds since any extension must send every $c/d$ to $f(c)f(d)^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0BSD, section-ramification, generic-fibre injectivity; explicit universal-property calculation

The delivery adds no new nodes and leaves the statement unchanged. There is no repair note, so the re-split rule does not apply; this is a first split of an unsplit node. The statement is true. I checked the last clause independently: ker f is a prime of C over (0), and the primes of C over (0) are the primes of S^{-1}C = L, a field, so ker f = 0. Step 1 identifies K⊗C with S^{-1}C and shows the map to L is injective (elementary). Step 2 uses lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability (base change, and ind-etale implies weakly etale) and lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field (every finitely generated k-subalgebra is finite etale); both statements say exactly what the step takes. This matches Stacks more-algebra Tag 092Q, lines 30504ff. Step 3 uses lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product: K[b] is a product of finite separable fields, and a nonzero domain forces exactly one factor. Step 4: B is a field, and the minimal polynomial does not change from K[b] to B, which gives separable algebraic in the sense of the definition node. Step 5: surjectivity via c/d = j((c/1)(d/1)^{-1}). Step 6: the extension h exists by the universal property of localization, is injective because B is a field, and is unique. I tested A=C, A a field, Z→Z[1/2], k[t]→k[t]^h, Z→Z_(p)^{sh}, and a non-domain A×A (correctly excluded). The citer lem-dl-a1-henselian-global-inertia-comparison step 2 uses only the stated clauses.
